Section 1

Product overview

LNMO is a cloud School ERP for Indian K-12 schools. One platform runs many schools; each school gets its admin console, staff workspace and parent/student portals — on desktop and mobile.

Key benefits

One-hour setup
Guided wizard, CSV imports and presets.
Smart timetable
Clash-free generation in seconds.
Fees without a gateway
Receipts, day book, defaulters, UPI QR and proofs — money goes straight to the school.
Parents onboard easily
OTP invites or paper slips.
Division-scoped principals
Each principal sees only their part of the school.
Audit everything
No hard deletes; every change is traceable.

Section 2

Multi-school isolation & security

  • Strict tenant isolation: every record carries its school's ID and every query is filtered by it. A user of one school cannot see or change another school's data, even by guessing links.
  • Role and scope checks on the server: principals are limited to their divisions, teachers to their classes/subjects, parents to their own children — enforced on every API call, not just hidden in the menu.
  • Secure sign-in: passwords are hashed; sessions use secure, HTTP-only cookies; brute-force protection on login.
  • Private files: photos, payment screenshots and attachments are stored in private object storage and served only to authorised users.
  • No silent changes: payments are reversed with credit notes rather than deleted; promotions can be rolled back; the audit log records who did what and when.
  • Messaging controls: templates and credits are approved by the platform; this demo runs in STUB mode.
Section 3

Platform Manager: onboard a new school

Who: LNMO Platform Manager

Create and manage schools (tenants), plans, messaging credits and support from one console. Each school's data is completely isolated.

Steps

  1. Sign in at /login with the platform manager account.
  2. Open Tenancy → Institutions and click “New Institution”.
  3. Enter the school name, code, domain, city and contact details, plus the first Institution Admin's name, login email and password.
  4. Click Create. The school appears in the list and its admin can sign in immediately at /login/<school-slug>.
  5. Use Plans to define subscription tiers, Communication to approve SMS/WhatsApp credit requests, and Issues to triage support tickets and app crash reports.
  6. Open a school → Features / AI to switch on the AI Tutor layer for that school only.
Tips
  • Passwords are never shown again after creation — the admin can reset them from their profile.
  • Every platform action is written to the Audit Log.
Section 4

Institution Admin onboarding

Who: Institution Admin

Set the school up in about an hour: profile, academic structure, staff, principals and students.

Steps

  1. Sign in at /login/<school-slug>. A fresh school opens the Setup wizard, which tracks each step.
  2. Settings → school profile, logo and seal (used on receipts, report cards and print views).
  3. Academic Years: create the year (e.g. 2026-27) with start/end dates. Academic Units: create divisions such as Primary and High School.
  4. Class Hub: classes, sections, class teachers and the subject teacher for every section; Subjects: the subject catalogue (bulk import supported).
  5. Teachers: add staff; mark a teacher as Principal and scope them to one or more divisions — they only ever see those classes.
  6. Students: add one by one or import from CSV; each student gets an admission number and is enrolled in the active year.
Tips
  • Principal scoping is by division: a High School principal cannot open Primary classes, fees or reports.
  • Use Users to deactivate accounts — records are never hard-deleted.
Section 5

Parent onboarding (OTP & paper invite slips)

Who: Admin / Principal → Parent

Get every parent onto the parent portal, whether or not a phone number is on file.

Steps

  1. Students page → Invite parents: parents with a phone number receive a WhatsApp/SMS invite link and verify with an OTP.
  2. For families without a phone on file, print paper setup slips (one per student, with a one-time setup code).
  3. The parent opens /setup/parent, enters the code or link, sets a password and is linked to their child (multiple children are supported).
  4. Track pending/accepted invites and send reminders from the same screen.
Tips
  • In this demo, SMS/WhatsApp run in STUB (demo) mode: messages are logged in history, not delivered.
Section 6

Class Hub — page by page

Who: Admin · Principal (own divisions); teachers use the results in their workspace

Class Hub is where a grade is defined: its sections, students, subjects, teachers, class teacher and leaders, and its timetable. Almost every other module reads from it.

Class Hub home (Academics → Class Hub)

A selector rail groups classes by academic unit and shows sections · students · subjects for each. Pick a class to see summary cards (unit, section class teachers, sections, subjects offered, attendance model inherited from the unit and whether a timetable is required) and an “Open class page” link. Below are five tabs; when a class is selected each tab shows only that class and new rows are added to it automatically.

Classes

Create classes (e.g. Grade 8), link each to an academic unit and grade level; edit or remove.

Use cases: Start of year: add Grade 10 under High School. · Move a class to the right unit so its principal and bell schedule apply.

Sections

Sections of the class with capacity, room and class teacher.

Use cases: Add Section C when admissions grow. · Record the room so it shows on the section page and timetable.

Enrollments

Which student is in which class and section for which academic year.

Use cases: Place a mid-year admission into 8B. · Check a section's roll before printing attendance registers.

Teacher Assignments

Teacher ↔ class/section/subject rows (also written by Subjects & Teachers).

Use cases: Give a new Hindi teacher Grade 8 A and B. · Audit who teaches what before marks entry opens.

Subject Offerings

Subjects offered to the class or to one section, with max marks or theory + practical split; “Bulk-offer a subject” adds one subject to many classes at once.

Use cases: Offer Computer Science with 70 + 30 practical marks. · Bulk-offer Value Education to every Primary class.

Class page (Open class page)

Overview

A card per section with class teacher, room, student and subject counts, plus quick links. Click a card to open the section page.

Use cases: Principal's morning glance at Grade 8. · Spot a section with no class teacher.

Sections & Staff

Add/rename sections; per section choose the class teacher, class leader and second leader (students), and the “Class teacher takes Period 1” switch. You are warned if a teacher already leads two sections.

Use cases: Appoint Aarav as 8A class leader. · Turn on Period 1 for the class teacher before generating the timetable.

Subjects & Teachers

The grade grid of subjects × sections: teacher per section, periods/week, consecutive, must, flexible (min–max); offer or remove a subject per section.

Use cases: Make Science a double period (Consec. 2, Must on). · Replace a subject teacher mid-term.

Students

Students with section, leader badges and achievement counts; add achievements (title, details, date) shown in an achievements table.

Use cases: Record Aarav's science-fair prize. · Class teacher checks the roll and leaders.

Timetable

The grade grid embedded for this class, with “Open full editor”.

Use cases: Quickly fix one period from the class page. · Show a parent the 8A week during a meeting.

Section page (click a section card)

Section 8 A

Header with class teacher, room, capacity and “Period 1 reserved” badge; Edit staff; Monthly Report (homework and assignment completion per student for a month); tabs Subjects & Teachers, Students and Timetable for just this section.

Use cases: Class teacher reviews who has not submitted homework this month. · Edit the section's room or class teacher in one place.

How Class Hub connects to other modules

Attendance. Registers list the students enrolled in each section; the unit's attendance model is inherited; class teachers mark attendance from their workspace.

Homework and assignments. Teachers post to the sections and subjects they are assigned; the section Monthly Report summarises completion.

Exams and marks. Offerings set max marks (theory/practical); teacher assignments decide who may enter marks for a subject and section.

Timetable and substitutions. Offerings, teachers, periods/week, consecutive/flexible rules and the Period 1 switch feed the generator; assignments drive cover suggestions.

Fees. Fee structures apply to a unit or class, so enrolment decides which students get invoices; the class teacher sees defaulters for their own section.

Parents and students. Portals show the child's class and section, subjects, timetable, homework and results from these records.

Principals. Scope is by academic unit, so the class's unit decides which principal can see and manage it.

Teachers don't open Class Hub. What is set here appears in their My Class, My Students, Marks Entry, Attendance, Homework and My Timetable.
Section 7

Smart Timetable — how it works

Who: Admin · Principal (own divisions) · Teachers, students and parents view

Build a clash-free weekly timetable for every grade from the subjects, teachers and weekly periods set in Class Hub, review it as a draft, publish it, and cover absent teachers day by day.

1. Concepts

Bell schedule and working days. Timetable → Setup, per academic year. Every period has a label, start and end time and a Break flag; nothing can ever be scheduled in a break. There is an institution default and an optional override per academic unit (for example a shorter day for Primary). At least one working day and one teaching period are required. Sunrise uses Monday–Saturday with P1, P2, Break, P3, P4, Lunch, P5, P6: 6 teaching periods × 6 days = 36 slots a week per section.

Subject offerings. A subject can only be timetabled for a section that is offered it (Class Hub). Sections of one grade can differ — e.g. Computer Science only in 8A.

Teacher per section and weekly periods. Class Hub → class → Subjects & Teachers: for each subject, the teacher of each section, Periods/wk, Consec. (1–3 periods in a row), Must (the block must be consecutive) and Flexible (with a min–max range). Teacher picks are saved as teacher assignments and drive marks entry and substitution suggestions as well.

Requirements check. Timetable → Requirements is a read-only summary per grade with a capacity badge (e.g. “30 / 36 periods·week (6d × 6p)”). Edit values in Class Hub.

Class teacher takes Period 1. A per-section switch (Class Hub → Sections & Staff). The generator then reserves P1 each working day for the class teacher's subject (the one with the most periods/week).

Flexible subjects and Auto-balance. Physical education, art, music, library, life skills, value education and similar subjects are flexible by default (you can change this per subject). With “Auto-balance flexible subjects” ticked, the generator trims flexible subjects (largest first, never below min) when a week is over-full, tops up empty slots with flexible subjects up to max, and—only for flexible subjects—may relax a consecutive rule. Saved requirements are never changed; every adjustment is listed in the report.

Rules the generator always respects

  • A teacher is never double-booked: the generator checks the published timetables of all other grades and everything it has already placed in this run.
  • One subject per section per slot; nothing in breaks; only subjects offered to that section.
  • Consecutive blocks are placed in truly adjacent teaching periods (never across a break) and at most one block per day per pass, so they spread across the week.
  • Single periods are spread day by day (round robin) instead of piling up on one day.
  • If a subject has a teacher pool rather than one section teacher, the least-loaded free teacher is chosen.
Not available today: per-teacher maximum periods per day/week, “teacher unavailable” slots, fixed slots other than the Period 1 rule, and automatic room allocation (rooms are only clash-checked when you place a period by hand).

2. Set up → generate → review → publish

  1. Setup: pick the academic year (and optionally a unit), tick working days, add periods and breaks with times, Save.
  1. Class Hub → Grade → Subjects & Teachers: offer subjects, pick a teacher per section, set periods/week and consecutive/flexible rules, Save changes.
  1. Timetable → Requirements: check that each grade fits its weekly capacity before generating.
  1. Grade grid → pick the grade → (optional) tick Auto-balance → Generate draft. One draft covers every section of the grade. Regenerating wipes and rebuilds the draft only; the published timetable is untouched until you publish.
  2. Read the report: periods placed per section, and anything that could not be placed with its cause — No teacher (placed unstaffed), Consecutive block impossible, Week full, Every teacher busy, or Class-teacher Period 1 shortfall — each with a one-click fix link into Class Hub.
  1. Edit by hand: click a cell to set subject, teacher and room; drag a period onto another slot to move it, or onto an occupied slot to swap the two. Every conflict is listed — hard ones (section already has a period, teacher double-booked, room in use) and soft ones (teacher not in the subject's pool, consecutive rule broken, Period 1 reserved for the class teacher). Cancel, or “Save anyway” — overridden cells get a ⚠ flag and the audit log records an OVERRIDE.
  1. Approve (optional) and Publish. Publishing replaces the grade's live timetable; teachers of that grade and in-scope admins/principals get a bell notification. Unpublish hides it from students and parents until you publish again.

3. Views

  • Grade grid — per section, with Published/Draft switch and a “View a date” overlay that shows that day's substitutions.
  • Builder — strict per-section manual builder.
  • By teacher — a teacher's week and number of periods.
  • By subject — every period of a subject across classes.
  • By day — the whole school for one weekday.
  • Teacher's My Timetable — weekly template or a specific date with cover periods.
  • Student and parent portal — the published weekly timetable (it does not show day-to-day substitutions).

4. Substitutions in depth

Marking an absence

  • Admin or principal: Substitutions → Mark absent → teacher, date, reason. It is approved at once and the system reads that teacher's published periods for that weekday, creating one cover slot per period (“Needs cover”). A principal can only mark teachers who teach in their divisions and only gets cover slots for their classes.
  • Teacher: My Substitutions → Request leave. Admins and in-scope principals are notified and see it under “Leave requests awaiting approval”; Approve creates the cover slots, Reject notifies the teacher.
  • An absence is for a whole day; a second absence for the same teacher and date is refused.

How substitutes are suggested

  1. Excluded: teachers teaching (published) in that period, teachers already covering another class then, teachers absent that day, and the absent teacher.
  2. Ranked by subject match: “Teaches this subject to this section”, then “Teaches this subject”, then “Available (other subject)”.
  3. Then by fewest substitutions already that day, then fewest periods that weekday, then name.

Assigning, asking and notifying

  • Assign: the period becomes “Covered” and the substitute gets a bell notification “Substitution assigned”.
  • Ask selected: tick several teachers; each gets a “Substitution request” notification and answers Accept or Decline in My Substitutions. Managers are notified of each answer; the answer appears in the suggestion list and you then click Assign.
  • Auto-cover all: assigns the best free teacher to every open slot of that absence (subject match first, then name) and reports how many stayed unstaffed. Use Find cover when you want the load-aware ranking.
  • Change: reopen suggestions for a covered period and assign someone else.

What the substitute sees

History and records

  • Pick any past date on the Substitutions page to see who was absent and who covered.
  • Each teacher's My assigned cover keeps their list of covers.
  • Every absence, approval, request, assignment and auto-cover is in the Audit Log. There is no separate substitution report or export yet.

Edge cases

No free teacher. The dialog says “No free teachers at this period” and Auto-cover leaves the slot open, reported as unstaffed.

Partial-day absence. Not modelled: an absence covers the whole day. Cover only the periods that need it; the others stay listed as “Needs cover”.

Cancelling. The system can cancel an absence — every linked cover is cancelled and the substitutes and asked teachers are notified — but the Substitutions screen has no Cancel button yet.

Day with no periods. If the teacher has no published periods that weekday, the absence shows “nothing to cover”.

5. Use cases

A teacher calls in sick at 7:30 AM. Substitutions → Mark absent (today, “Fever”). The day's periods appear instantly. Press Auto-cover all, or Find cover for each period to use the load-aware ranking. Substitutes get notified and see the cover on My Timetable before the first bell.

Planned leave tomorrow. The teacher uses Request leave; the principal approves on the Substitutions page (pick tomorrow's date) and arranges cover a day ahead.

Mid-term change of subject teacher. Class Hub → Grade → Subjects & Teachers → choose the new teacher for the section → Save. This updates assignments, marks entry and suggestions. Published periods keep the old name until you change those cells in the Grade grid, or regenerate and publish the grade.

A new section is added. Class Hub → Sections & Staff → add Section C with class teacher and room; Subjects & Teachers → offer subjects and teachers; Timetable → Generate draft for the grade (all its sections are re-planned) → review → Publish.

Exam week. Exam papers are scheduled under Exams (see the Exams section), not in the weekly timetable, which stays published. Teachers away on exam duty can be marked absent for those days and covered.

Different bell for Primary. Setup → choose the Primary unit → set its own periods and working days → Save. Generation and checks for Primary classes use that override.

6. Tips and FAQ

  • Check Requirements first: if total periods exceed slots, the report will show “Week full”.
  • Give popular subjects a teacher pool, not just one teacher, so the generator has room to avoid clashes.
  • Use Draft mode to experiment; nothing is visible to teachers, students or parents until you publish.
  • Overrides are allowed but flagged ⚠ — fix them before term starts.
Will regenerating overwrite my published timetable?

No. It replaces only the draft for that grade. The live timetable changes when you press Publish.

Can a principal generate timetables?

Yes, for classes in their divisions only — the same scope applies to edits, publishing and substitutions.

Why was a period placed without a teacher?

The subject is offered but no teacher is assigned for that section; the report links straight to Subjects & Teachers.

Do parents see substitutions?

No. Students and parents see the published weekly timetable; cover is shown to staff.

Does it limit how many periods a teacher gets per day?

Not as a hard limit. It avoids clashes and picks the least-loaded teacher from a pool; use the By teacher view to check loads.

Section 8

Exams, assessments and report cards

Who: Admin / Principal / Teacher

Plan an exam timetable per division, collect marks from subject teachers and publish results and report cards.

Steps

  1. Exams → New exam: name, type and a date window plus time slots for each division.
  2. Generate the exam schedule (no student sits two papers at once) and the mark registers.
  3. Teachers enter marks in Marks Entry; after publishing, only a principal/admin can correct marks (audited).
  4. Publish results: students and parents see marks and report cards; report cards can also be sent to parents.
Tips
  • Results here are visible to students and parents only after Publish results.

Section 10

AI Tutor

Who: Student (managed by Admin / Teacher)

A safe AI study companion aligned to the school's curriculum; teachers can review and comment on curriculum content.

Steps

  1. Platform Manager switches on the AI Layer for the school (Institution → Features / AI).
  2. Teachers add chapters, notes and textbook material for their class and subject under AI Tutor, then submit the curriculum.
  3. The admin or principal approves it under AI Tutor → Pending curricula, and turns the AI Tutor on for that curriculum in the Curricula browser.
  4. Student portal → AI Tutor: pick the subject and ask a question; answers come from the approved curriculum, step by step.
Tips
  • Subjects without an approved curriculum show “Not enabled yet” to students.
Section 11

Fees

Who: Admin (collection also by Principals for their divisions)

End-to-end offline fee management: structures, ledgers, receipts, day book, defaulters and reminders, monthly reports, UPI QR and payment proofs.

Steps

  1. Structures: define fee heads per division and year (term/monthly/one-time, late fee), apply to students and generate invoices.
  2. Accounts → Ledger: every invoice and payment for a student; set concessions; download the statement PDF.
  3. Collect: amount, method (cash/UPI/cheque/bank), reference and payment date (backdating allowed, audited). A numbered receipt and PDF are issued instantly.
  4. Day Book: the day's collection by method, collector and class; print for the daily cash closing.
  5. Defaulters: overdue students with ageing buckets; one-tap or bulk reminders (max one per student per day); CSV and print.
  6. Monthly Summary: billed vs collected per class, previous dues, collection %, printable management report.
  7. UPI: enable in Settings → UPI payments; parents see a QR for the exact balance and upload a screenshot (“I've paid”).
  8. Payment proofs: staff approve (creates a normal receipt dated on the payment date) or reject with a reason; parent “I have already paid” issues are handled in the same tab.
Tips
  • To reverse a wrong receipt use the ↺ action in the ledger: the payment is kept and flagged with a credit note — never deleted.
  • Unpaid balances carry forward automatically as “Previous dues” at year-end promotion.

Communications

Notices, WhatsApp/SMS messages, templates and message history in one place.

Steps

Section 13

Promotion / Rollover

Who: Admin (whole-school principal)

Move every student to the next year in one auditable run, with recommendations from class teachers.

Steps

  1. Promotion → choose from-year and to-year → Preview: each student gets a decision (promote, detain, graduate, transfer).
  2. Students with unpaid fees show “Dues pending ₹X” and a summary banner — a warning only, promotion is not blocked.
  3. Execute after typing the confirmation. Unpaid balances move to the new year as a “Previous dues” invoice (idempotent, linked to originals). A rollback is available.

Who: Admin / Principal / Teacher

Daily operations that round out the ERP.

Steps

Portal tours: principal, teacher, parent and student

Who: Each role

What each person sees after signing in.

Steps

Glossary

Institution / tenantOne school. Its data is isolated from every other school.
Division / Academic unitA group of classes such as Primary or High School; principals are scoped by division.
Day BookThe daily collection register used for cash closing.
DefaulterA student with an invoice past its due date and an unpaid balance.
Previous dues / arrearsUnpaid balance carried into the next academic year at promotion.
UTRThe 12-digit UPI/bank transaction reference.
Payment proofA parent-uploaded payment screenshot awaiting staff verification.
STUB modeDemo messaging: messages are logged but not delivered.

FAQ

How do I collect cash?

Fees → Accounts → open the student's Ledger → Collect on the invoice → method Cash, amount, payment date → Record. Print or download the receipt.

How do I reverse a payment?

Open the Ledger, click ↺ on the receipt and enter a reason. The receipt is kept, marked reversed with a credit-note number, and the balance is restored.

A parent paid by UPI — how is it recorded?

The parent uploads the screenshot with “I've paid”. In Fees → Payment proofs, approve it (edit the amount/UTR if needed); a normal UPI receipt is created on the payment date.

Can a principal see other divisions?

No. Every list, report, fee action and export is filtered to the divisions assigned to that principal.

Is data ever deleted?

Operational records are never hard-deleted: they are deactivated, reversed or rolled back with an audit trail.
